summary:
I found one low-severity issue in Task L and nothing more serious. I reviewed the full diffs of drive_v3.py, train_backbone_v3.py, run_pool_rollout_v3.py, commit_v3.py (find_policy_caches only), check_caches_v3.py, run_repairs_v3.py, hpc/dry_run_v3.sh, hpc/README_v3.md and tests/test_hpc_v3.py, and read tests/test_checkpoint_tag_v3.py in full. I also read the unchanged hpc/backbone_v3.slurm, hpc/rollout_v3.slurm, hpc/cells_v3.txt, scripts/repair_experiment.py and the Task L section of instruction_round3.md.

Tests: I ran the four required files myself (tests/test_checkpoint_tag_v3.py, tests/test_hpc_v3.py, tests/test_v3_scripts.py, tests/test_multisplit_v3.py): `33 passed in 133.85s (0:02:13)`.

Unchanged outputs, checked against the HEAD versions loaded from `git show` (everything written to scratchpad/review_L only):
- drive_v3 --dry-run gives byte-identical output to HEAD for all four phases, seeds 0-2, with no extra flags, with --tag, and with --commit-prefix / --metrics-dir-name (12 combinations, 0 differences).
- run_repairs_v3 --dry-run gives identical output for three label/seed combinations.
- commit_v3.find_policy_caches returns identical results for all 49 caches in pool_v2 and pool_v3, and no existing policy token contains "-".
- check_caches_v3 on the real pool_v3 (with --v2-dir and --csv) and on pool_v2 gives identical stdout, an identical CSV and rc 0.

Tagged path and cluster plumbing:
- Tagged dry runs on the real roots print checkpoints_v3_repair/fashionmnist_ts0.pt and the two -repair cache paths.
- The commit and sweep phases reject --checkpoint-tag with exit 2.
- hpc/dry_run_v3.sh with BB_INDICES=6, RO_INDICES="12 13", BB_EXTRA and DRY_DRIVER_FLAGS on the real roots shows the overrides and --checkpoint-tag reaching train_backbone_v3 and run_pool_rollout_v3. Without those variables the same indices still print "skip (exists)".
- Indices 6 / 12 / 13 map to fashionmnist seed 0 (backbone 6 % 8 = 6; cells_v3.txt 0-based lines 12 and 13 are fashionmnist greedy_entropy and random, seed 0).
- In the README §8 wall-time table, each figure matches ledger × 4 (× 2 for epochs) ÷ 1.4178, using handoff §6 values 1602.9 / 14565.1 / 308.2.
- The rollout loads width_mult from the checkpoint's meta["arch"], so a width-4 checkpoint loads correctly.
- repair_experiment.py writes results_v3/repair/fashionmnist_ts0_{label}.json, the same path run_repairs_v3 checks for fashionmnist.
- The helper scripts stay torch-free: importing check_caches_v3, run_repairs_v3, drive_v3 and commit_v3 does not load torch.

Tests are not vacuous: the old check_caches grouping would fail the two-pair assertion, and a non-skipping find_policy_caches would fail the lambda_refs equality check.

The one finding: an empty tag (`--checkpoint-tag ""` / `--repair-tag ""`) is silently treated as "no tag". It cannot happen through the documented driver or Slurm lines (the driver skips an existing checkpoint). A direct train_backbone_v3 call with an empty tag (for example a bash variable that expanded to "") plus the width/p_full overrides overwrites the protocol seed-0 checkpoint. I reproduced this in a tmp root.

Other points I checked, already disclosed by the implementer and not defects of the spec:
- --labels is ignored under --repair-tag.
- The repair labels are fixed whatever the tag.
- Dashed eps_greedy tokens below 1e-4 are now rejected.
- The time estimates for the greedy rollout (11-16 h) conflict with the user's "about 1-2 GPU hours".
- The 24 h TinyGPU limit is not confirmed.

findings.title: Empty checkpoint/repair tag is silently treated as untagged; train_backbone_v3 with overrides then overwrites the protocol seed-0 backbone
findings.evidence:
validate_checkpoint_tag maps "" to None (drive_v3.py:74-75), and checkpoint_tag_arg is the argparse type= for --checkpoint-tag / --repair-tag. So an explicitly given empty tag means 'no tag' with no error.

1) In scratchpad/review_L/empty_tag.py, with a tmp RESULTS_ROOT holding a fake protocol checkpoints_v3/fashionmnist_ts0.pt, a monkeypatched load_pool_v3 and CPU, I ran train_backbone_v3.main([... '--checkpoint-tag', '', '--width-mult', '1', '--p-full', '0.3', '--epochs', '1']). Output: `rc 0 protocol ckpt sha 807b669cecd3 -> 9cff3a6e321a | meta checkpoint_tag None arch {'name': 'masked_cnn_v2', 'width_mult': 1, 'n_classes': 10} | tagged dir exists: False`. The protocol checkpoint was overwritten by a non-protocol backbone, and its meta does not mark it as one. train_backbone_v3 has no exists-check, so a direct call (as in its own docstring example) with `--checkpoint-tag "$TAG"` and TAG unset does the same on the real root.

2) `run_repairs_v3.py --seeds 0 --datasets fashionmnist --repair-tag "" --dry-run --force` prints `would run repair:fashionmnist:policy_change:ts0 ...`. It silently falls back to the round-2 job list, and without --dry-run that would overwrite results_v3/repair/fashionmnist_ts0_policy_change.json.

The documented driver and Slurm routes are safe, because drive_v3 skips the existing protocol checkpoint ('skip (exists)').
findings.suggested_fix: In checkpoint_tag_arg, reject "" (raise ArgumentTypeError 'empty tag'), so only an omitted flag means untagged; keep validate_checkpoint_tag(None/"") -> None for internal callers. Optionally, in train_backbone_v3.main, refuse --width-mult / --p-full without --checkpoint-tag (p.error), or refuse to overwrite an existing checkpoints_v3/{ds}_ts{ts}.pt when any override is given. Either way a non-protocol backbone can never land in the protocol folder.
